restatements.text: Allows parents of children eligible for public school to open an education savings account, into which the state will deposit 90 percent of the per-pupil funding that would have gone to the child's resident public school district.
Permits funds in the education savings account to be spent on private school tuition, tutoring, textbooks, and approved online courses.

findings.quote: A parent of a child eligible to attend public school may open an education savings account. The state shall deposit into the account 90 percent of the state per-pupil funding
findings.mechanism: Provides public funding for education alternatives by establishing education savings accounts funded by state per-pupil dollars.

findings.quote: Account funds may be used for private school tuition, tutoring, textbooks, and approved online courses.
findings.mechanism: Legally authorizes the use of state funds for private schools and other alternative educational services.

findings.quote: The state shall deposit into the account 90 percent of the state per-pupil funding the child's resident district would otherwise receive.
findings.mechanism: Reduces the resources available to district public schools by redirecting 90 percent of a participating student's per-pupil funding away from the resident district.

findings.quote: A parent of a child eligible to attend public school may open an education savings account.
findings.mechanism: Increases parents' direct authority over their children's education by giving them control of state education funds.

analysis.answer: Under current law, state education funds go exclusively to public school districts and charter schools. This measure redirects 90 percent of a participating student's state per-pupil funding to a savings account controlled by the parent.

The state incurs the direct cost of depositing 90 percent of per-pupil funding into the accounts. If children already attending private schools or being homeschooled are deemed "eligible to attend public school," the state will bear substantial new costs by subsidizing students who previously did not use state education funds.

Parents who choose private or alternative education benefit from the state subsidy. Private schools, tutors, and educational vendors benefit from the new revenue stream. Public school districts bear the cost of lost per-pupil funding for departing students.

Parents may increasingly withdraw their children from public schools to utilize the funds for private alternatives. Private educational providers may expand capacity or increase tuition prices to capture the newly available state funds. Public school districts may struggle to reduce their fixed overhead costs at the same rate they lose enrollment revenue.

The measure addresses parents' lack of financial access to alternative education by providing portable funding. However, it may create budget instability for public school districts if a critical mass of students departs, removing revenue without equally reducing the districts' operating costs.
Parents gain discretion over how their child's share of state education funding is spent. Private school administrators and education service vendors gain market power and revenue.

The effects of education savings accounts and vouchers are heavily disputed. Some researchers find they introduce healthy competition that improves outcomes across all schools and gives marginalized students better opportunities; others find they drain vital resources from public systems and fail to improve test scores for the participating students.
The state will incur administrative costs to establish the accounting system, disburse funds, verify that expenditures match the allowed categories, and evaluate or approve online courses.

flags.note: The measure does not establish an approval mechanism or criteria, meaning the real effect depends on future agency rules or appointments to define which courses qualify.

items.text: Expands public funding and legal options for educational alternatives like private school and tutoring.
Increases parents' authority to direct their children's education using state funds.
Reduces per-pupil funding available to district public schools when students utilize the savings accounts.

changes.empty_reason: No directional concerns were affected by the measure.

items.text: Maintains 100 percent of state per-pupil funding within the public school and charter system.
Forgoes the creation of state-funded education savings accounts for private tuition and alternative schooling.
Forgoes expanding parents' direct financial control over state education funds.
